<!-- Source: docs/authors/knowledge-sources.md -->

# Knowledge Sources

> **Audience:** Authors and operators grounding the AI in their own documents.

Workflows follow *your* runbooks and policies instead of generic knowledge. When
a workflow gets your data-retention rule right, it is because the runbook was a
Knowledge Source the AI read while writing it — which also means the evidence a
review will ask for is produced as you work, not reconstructed months later.

A Knowledge Source is a persistent, indexed document store the AI can search
while authoring, discovering, or repairing workflows. For the conceptual model —
and how Knowledge Sources differ from Skills — see
[Knowledge & Skills](../concepts/knowledge-and-skills.md).

## How grounding works

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    src[Your docs<br/>runbooks, policies, specs] --> ingest[Ingest<br/>upload, crawl, scheduled refresh]
    ingest --> chunk[Chunk<br/>split into searchable passages]
    chunk --> embed[Embed and index<br/>vectors + tags]
    embed --> search[Hybrid search<br/>semantic + tag filter]
    search --> ground[Grounds authoring<br/>follows your rules, not generic knowledge]
    ground --> wf[Authored / repaired workflow]
```

| Stage | What happens |
|---|---|
| Ingest | Upload, crawl, or scheduled refresh pulls the document in. |
| Chunk | The text is split into searchable passages. |
| Embed + index | Passages become vectors; tags and descriptions are attached. |
| Hybrid search | Queries rank by semantic relevance, narrowed by tag. |
| Ground | Matched passages enter the authoring context so the workflow follows your rules. |

---

## Adding a source

In the REPL, say *"add this file as a knowledge source tagged weather, runbook"*.
The scriptable form:

```bash
sk knowledge-sources create --file ./runbook.md \
  --title "Weather Runbook" --tags "weather,runbook,open-meteo"
sk knowledge-sources list
sk knowledge-sources search "open-meteo"   # semantic search; ranks by relevance
```

| Flag | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `--tags` | Authoritative — no AI auto-tagging when you supply them. |
| `--description` | Authoritative when supplied. |
| (omit both) | The engine generates tags and a description. |

## Auto-analysis and self-description

When a document is uploaded interactively — from chat, an attached file, or
`sk knowledge-sources create` — the AI auto-analyzes its content to generate a
short description and a set of topical tags. This makes each source
self-describing: the AI can list sources and decide which one covers a topic
before searching, and a search can be narrowed to sources carrying a given tag.

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Description | Generated only when none was supplied. |
| Tags | Topical tags are a deduped set that re-analysis replaces wholesale; **namespaced tags** (a name-shaped prefix — letters/digits, Unicode included — a colon, and content directly after it: `domain:blog-de`, `café:paris`) are structural routing keys that always survive re-analysis, and re-analysis never adds new ones. Prose or punctuation colons (`note: x`, `q&a:faq`) stay topical. The `<ns>:` shape is reserved for routing, so don't use it for plain topical tags. To re-home a source (drop or change a `domain:*` tag), edit the tags explicitly (`sk knowledge-sources update` / PATCH) — explicit edits replace the tag set wholesale. |
| Embeddings | Freshly ingested or updated chunks are embedded right away (source-scoped, off the request path); semantic ranking works within seconds of an update, no manual step needed. |
| Failure mode | Best-effort — if it fails (e.g. model budget exhausted) the upload still succeeds, just without enrichment. |
| Re-run | `sk knowledge-sources analyze <id>`, or the `analyze_knowledge_source` tool in chat. |
| Bulk paths | Crawled pages and scheduled refreshes stay mechanical — not auto-analyzed. |

## Importing a whole directory (knowledge bundles)

A team wiki rarely lives in one file. `import` turns a directory of markdown
files — an Obsidian vault, an agent-maintained wiki, a Notion export, or an
[OKF](https://okf.md/) bundle — into **one** knowledge source with one
searchable passage per file:

```bash
sk knowledge-sources import ./team-wiki --tags "runbooks"
```

In the REPL the same import is `/knowledge import ./team-wiki` — ask a question
right after and the answer grounds on your wiki.

> **Importing for a coding agent?** Tag the source with the domain, or a Claude
> Code / Codex session will never see it: `sk knowledge-sources import ./team-wiki
> --tags "domain:<slug>"`. The session briefing indexes exactly the sources
> carrying its `domain:` tag — see [Use sk from a coding agent](./coding-agents.md).

| Behavior | Detail |
|---|---|
| Upsert by slug | Re-running the import is idempotent: unchanged content reports `unchanged`, changed content re-ingests in place. Perfect for a CI job that keeps sk in sync with a git wiki. |
| Frontmatter | Read tolerantly, never rejected. `type: Runbook` becomes a structural `type:runbook` tag (filterable in search); a `tags:` list merges into the source's topical tags. Files without frontmatter import fine. |
| Reserved files | `index.md` and `log.md` (navigation/history in OKF bundles) are skipped at any depth. |
| Reading it back | `read_knowledge` (chat/MCP tool) pages through the full content — e.g. *"read me the deploy runbook"* after a search hit; `GET /v1/knowledge-sources/{id}/chunks` is the raw HTTP form. Nothing is locked in. |

Pairing with a knowledge-engineering system that exports OKF bundles: schedule
a workflow that pulls the exported bundle and posts it to
`POST /v1/knowledge-sources/bundle` — curated knowledge lands in sk as governed
grounding: every read is RBAC-gated (`knowledge:read`), and every import that
writes anything is audited (an unchanged re-import is a deliberate no-op).

## Refresh strategies and scope

Knowledge Sources have configurable refresh strategies, so the AI always works
from current documentation. When a runbook is updated, the source refreshes and
the next workflow follows the new rule.

| Axis | Options |
|---|---|
| Refresh | Manual or scheduled. |
| Scope | Tenant-wide (available globally) or pinned to specific workflows. |

## Budgets

Per-source and per-tenant byte caps, per-message file counts, and ingestion
concurrency are operator-tunable. Defaults are conservative; raise them on
hardware that warrants larger corpora. The full tunable table lives in
[Observability & Resource Limits → Documentation & Knowledge Tunables](../operators/observability.md#documentation--knowledge-tunables).

---

## Further reading

- [Use sk from a coding agent](./coding-agents.md) — grounding a coding agent in these sources: the `domain:` tag, the briefing, and the review loop.
- [Knowledge & Skills](../concepts/knowledge-and-skills.md) — the conceptual model and context-assembly order.
- [Model a Domain](./model-a-domain.md) — a Knowledge Source and a Skill configured side by side for one domain, worked end to end.
- [Custom Skills](./custom-skills.md) — the dense, prescriptive counterpart to Knowledge Sources.
- [AI-assisted authoring](./authoring-workflows.md) — how Conversations draw on Knowledge Sources.

<!-- Source: docs/authors/model-a-domain.md -->

# Model a Domain

> **Audience:** Authors and operators teaching sk about a whole field of work —
> a policy, a process, a specialized domain — not just a single workflow.

Teach sk a whole field of work once, and every workflow in it arrives right the
first time. The AI proposes against your conventions and looks the specifics up
in your own documents, so review stops being the place where the draft gets
fixed.

A single workflow answers one question. A **domain** — your expense policy, your
contract-review process, a compliance framework — is the shared context that
makes *every* workflow in it correct. You model a domain by standing up three
primitives around it: a **Connector**, one or more **Skills**, and one or more
**Knowledge Sources**. This guide shows the trio working together.

For the conceptual model behind the two context primitives, see
[Knowledge & Skills](../concepts/knowledge-and-skills.md). For the quick "which
one do I reach for?" answer, jump to the [FAQ](../concepts/faq.md).

---

## The trio

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C[Connector<br/>the domain's API / system of record] --> AI
    S[Skill<br/>house conventions the AI FOLLOWS] --> AI
    K[Knowledge Source<br/>reference docs the AI SEARCHES] --> AI
    AI([AI authors inside your domain]) --> W[Correct-by-construction workflow]
```

| Primitive | Its job in the domain | Prescribes or informs |
|---|---|---|
| **Connector** | Authenticate the domain's system once; ground requests against its real, discovered surface | — |
| **Skill** | Encode the rules the AI must obey — required validations, error handling, approval gates, tone | **Prescribes** |
| **Knowledge Source** | Hold the domain's reference material — policy PDFs, runbooks, glossaries, rate tables | **Informs** |

The mnemonic that keeps them straight: **Skills prescribe; Knowledge Sources
inform.** The decision table for borderline cases lives in
[Custom Skills](./custom-skills.md#authoring-and-scoping-a-skill) — reuse it
rather than guessing.

---

## Worked example: an expense-approval domain

Say your finance team wants sk to help build expense-handling automations that
always honor company policy. Model the domain once:

**1. Connector — the system of record.** Register the connector for wherever
expenses live (your accounting API, an HR system). This is the normal
connector-creation flow; the AI grounds every request against the connector's
discovered endpoints.

**2. Skill — the conventions the AI must follow.** Author a tight,
single-purpose Skill scoped to that connector (or global if it spans several).
It prescribes the rules, for example:

> Expenses over €1,000 require a second approver. Never auto-approve travel
> without an attached receipt. Reject line items with no cost-center code.

Author it in a Conversation, or from the CLI:

```bash
sk skills create --file ./expense-policy-skill.json   # a SkillDef JSON
sk skills list
```

Because it is prescriptive, the AI *follows* it — proposals that violate the
policy never get authored in the first place.

**3. Knowledge Source — the reference material.** Upload the actual policy so
the AI can cite specifics (thresholds, eligible categories, per-diem rates):

```bash
sk knowledge-sources create --file ./expense-policy-2026.pdf \
  --tags "expense,policy,finance"
sk knowledge-sources search "per-diem cap for international travel"
```

Or, in a Conversation, attach the document and say *"add this as a knowledge
source tagged expense, policy"* — sk creates it and (unless you supply them)
auto-generates a description and tags.

**The combined effect.** When someone now asks sk to build an
expense-reimbursement workflow, the AI proposes steps that respect the
two-approver rule (from the **Skill**) and fills in the correct per-diem figure
(from the **Knowledge Source**), grounded against your accounting API (the
**Connector**). The evidence a compliance review needs is produced as you work, not reconstructed afterwards.

---

## Chunk for retrieval: many focused sources beat one blob

Knowledge Sources are searched at the **chunk** level — the AI receives only the
passages that match the current question. Granularity is therefore a quality
lever. Split a domain's reference material into focused documents rather than one
giant file:

| Instead of | Prefer |
|---|---|
| `everything-about-expenses.pdf` (50 KB) | `per-diem-rates.md`, `approval-thresholds.md`, `eligible-categories.md` |

Sharper matches, less wasted context budget, and each source is independently
refreshable. See [Knowledge Sources](./knowledge-sources.md) for ingest,
tagging, and refresh strategies, and
[Knowledge & Skills → context assembly](../concepts/knowledge-and-skills.md#context-assembly-and-trimming)
for how the retrieved chunks are ordered and trimmed under budget.

---

## The pattern is domain-agnostic

Expense policy is just an instance. The identical trio models any field:

| Domain | Connector | Skill | Knowledge Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contract review | Your CLM / doc store | Clause-review conventions | Standard-clause library, redline policy |
| Tax filing | Tax authority API | Filing-rule conventions | Rate tables, deduction glossary |
| Music theory | (optional) score API | `music-theory-authoring` conventions | `harmonic-functions.md`, `chord-voicings.md`, glossary |

Whatever the field, the shape is the same: a Connector to ground requests,
Skills to prescribe how the work is done, Knowledge Sources to inform the
specifics.

---

## Further reading

- [Knowledge & Skills](../concepts/knowledge-and-skills.md) — the conceptual model and context-assembly order.
- [Custom Skills](./custom-skills.md) — how to author, scope, and promote Skills.
- [Knowledge Sources](./knowledge-sources.md) — how to upload, tag, and refresh documents.
- [FAQ](../concepts/faq.md) — quick answers on workflows, skills, and knowledge sources.

<!-- Source: docs/authors/quickstart.md -->

# Quickstart — Authors

In about five minutes you will have described a piece of work in ordinary sentences and
watched it run — no code written, nothing touched in a real system until you said so. You
describe the outcome; sk builds the connection, drafts the process, and holds every write
back until you approve it.

![Describing a workflow in plain language, previewing it, approving it, and running it](../_tapes/out/repl-author.gif)

## Your first conversation

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor You
    participant sk
    You->>sk: Describe the outcome in plain language
    sk-->>You: Proposes a workflow (connector + steps)
    You->>sk: /preview
    sk-->>You: Dry-run result, no writes
    You->>sk: /approve
    sk-->>You: Commits a versioned workflow
    You->>sk: Run it
    sk-->>You: Audited execution + result
```

Every step is permission-checked and recorded. Nothing writes to a real system until you approve.

## The first thing to try

Once connected (pick a path below), type a sentence, not a command. Two that work
immediately:

> *"Show me the top five repos of the vercel org by stars."*

Every fresh tenant already carries this as a seeded, credential-free demo workflow — so
your very first run succeeds before any system is connected. Then point at a system your
operator has connected:

> *"Every morning at 7, mail me our open Jira tickets grouped by assignee."*

sk proposes the workflow, `/preview` shows you the dry run with every write held back,
`/approve` commits it. More worth building, with what each case needs:
[Use cases](../use-cases.md).

## Connect

Your operator has given you **one** of the following. Pick the matching path.

- **Engine URL + API key** — you operate a tenant directly → Path A.
- **Portal-token link** — you are a scoped end-user → Path B.
- **Slack / Teams / Google Chat** where the sk bot is installed → Path C.
- **An MCP client** (Claude Desktop, Cursor, …) → Path D.
- **Claude Code or Codex** → [Use sk from a coding agent](./coding-agents.md) — the
  coding-agent loop needs a briefing hook and domain-tagged knowledge on top of
  the MCP registration, so it has its own page.

> **Want to run your own engine first?** [Self-host quickstart](../developers/self-host.md) takes you from the Docker image to a first connector and workflow.

## Path A — CLI with API key

```bash
curl -fsSL <URL>/install | bash          # the CLI is served by your engine
sk login --engine-url <URL> --api-key <wf_live_…>
sk                         # opens the TUI, picks up your session
```

## Path B — CLI with portal token

Portal tokens are time-limited and pre-scoped. Click the link your operator sent; it provisions a session for `sk` automatically.

```bash
sk login --portal-token <token>      # token is time-limited and pre-scoped; reusable until it expires or is revoked
sk
```

## Path C — Chat (Slack / Teams / Google Chat)

Nothing to install. In the workspace your operator set up:

- **Slack.** `@sk run <workflow>` or just `@sk …` to start a conversation.
- **Teams.** Same pattern — `@sk …` in a channel or DM.
- **Google Chat.** Invite the bot to a space; mention it.

See [input surfaces](../developers/input-surfaces.md) for how each chat adapter works.

## Path D — MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.)

Add the engine as a streamable-HTTP MCP server:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sk": {
      "url": "https://<engine-host>/mcp",
      "transport": "streamable-http",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <key>" }
    }
  }
}
```

Your client discovers workflows, prompts, and resources automatically. See [input surfaces](../developers/input-surfaces.md) for MCP details.

**Claude Code / Codex** register from the shell rather than a JSON file, and
want the briefing hook and domain-tagged knowledge as well — that whole path is
[Use sk from a coding agent](./coding-agents.md).

## Troubleshooting

Any failed request prints `{code}: {message} [trace=…]`. Send the `trace_id` to your operator — they correlate it with `sk diagnostics errors --trace-id <trace_id>`.

## Next steps

- [input surfaces](../developers/input-surfaces.md) — every surface: CLI, REST, MCP, chat, webhooks, schedules.
- [authoring workflows](./authoring-workflows.md) — what Conversations can do: proposing workflows, Skills, Knowledge Sources, Discovery, and the approval gate.
- [REPL tour](./repl-tour.md) — the authoring state machine and slash commands end to end.

<!-- Source: docs/authors/repl-tour.md -->

# Using the `sk` REPL — authoring by conversation

**Go from idea to a governed, versioned workflow in minutes** — no JSON, no
glue code. Describe the outcome in plain language; the AI proposes a connector
or workflow, previews a real result, and only commits when you approve. Every
saved artifact is permission-checked, audited, and replayable.

![Describing a workflow in plain language, previewing it, approving it, and running it](../_tapes/out/repl-author.gif)

This guide assumes you are already authenticated (see
[zero-to-running](../developers/self-host.md), Steps 1–2). Everything below also works
inside the container as `docker exec -it subkit sk …`.

---

## The authoring state machine

One conversation, one gate. The AI iterates on a draft as long as you want;
**approval is the only path to a saved, runnable workflow.**

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Describing
    Describing --> Proposing: AI has enough to draft
    Proposing --> Previewing: dry-run the draft
    Previewing --> Proposing: revise (reject / "change X")
    Previewing --> Committed: /approve
    Committed --> Running: sk workflows run
    Committed --> [*]
    Running --> [*]

    note right of Proposing
        AI proposes — nothing is
        saved or executed yet
    end note
    note right of Committed
        Versioned resource:
        audited, permission-checked,
        replayable
    end note
```

---

## Start a conversation

```bash
sk                      # opens the interactive REPL
sk "current weather in Berlin"   # opens the REPL with a first message
sk -c                   # continue your most recent conversation
sk -r <conversation-id> # resume a specific one
```

You type in natural language. The AI replies, and — when it has enough — it
**proposes** a connector or workflow as a structured draft. Nothing is saved or
executed until you approve.

---

## The authoring loop (what actually happens)

```
You    ▸ get the current temperature in Berlin
AI     ▸ I'll use the open-meteo connector (keyless). Here's the workflow I propose:
         1. request  GET /v1/forecast?latitude=52.52&longitude=13.41&current=temperature_2m
         2. transform extract { city, time, temperature_c }
         (shows the draft + a dry-run preview result: 21.4 °C)
         Approve to save this as a workflow?
You    ▸ /approve
AI     ▸ Saved workflow "berlin-current-temperature" (v1). Run it with: sk workflows run berlin-current-temperature
```

Key properties:

- **AI proposes, you approve.** The AI never commits a workflow or runs it in
  production on its own — approval is the governance gate.
- **Preview before save.** The proposal includes a dry-run so you see a real
  result before committing.
- **Iterate in place.** Reject or just say what to change (“also return
  windspeed”, “use Munich instead”) and the AI revises the draft.

---

## Slash commands

Type `/` for the live menu. The shipped commands:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/approve` | Approve the AI's current proposal (commit the draft). |
| `/reject` | Reject the proposal (optionally with a reason); the AI revises. |
| `/preview` | Dry-run the current workflow draft now (`/preview show` for the last result). |
| `/probe` | Test the current connector draft now (`/probe show` for the last result). |
| `/draft` · `/connector` · `/workflow` | Inspect the current authoring state. |
| `/templates` | Browse connector templates suggested for the draft. |
| `/onboard` | Guided wizard: pick a template, enter credentials, probe, save. |
| `/versions` · `/restore <n>` | List committed workflow versions / roll back to one. |
| `/skills` · `/knowledge` | List reusable Skills / knowledge sources in scope. |
| `/clear` (`/new`) · `/compact` · `/resume` | New conversation · shrink history · reattach. |
| `/setup` · `/status` · `/cost` · `/usage` | Readiness · session+persona · budget · token usage. |
| `/config` | Open the searchable Config tab (every engine setting). |
| `/settings` (`/preferences`) | Open the 5-tab settings palette (Status / Config / Usage / Skills / Knowledge). |
| `/model` · `/tenant` · `/login` · `/logout` | Switch model · switch/list tenants · auth. |
| `/attach` · `/upload` · `/files` | Attach a file to the message · upload · list files. |
| `/yolo` | Lift the destructive-action confirm gate for a few turns (typed `yes`). |
| `/help` · `/exit` (`/quit`) | Cheat sheet · leave the REPL. |

## Mentions & attachments

- `@file:<id>` — attach a previously uploaded file to the message.
- `@skill:<name>` — pull a specific Skill into context.
- Attach files when launching headless: `sk -p "build a connector from this" --attach ./openapi.json`.

---

## Example conversations to try

```
create a connector for the open-meteo forecast API (https://api.open-meteo.com), no auth
```
```
make a workflow that returns tomorrow's high and low for a city I pass as input
```
```
add a knowledge article from ./runbook.md tagged ops,weather
```
```
run berlin-current-temperature and show me the result
```

After `/approve`, the artifact is a normal, versioned resource — manage it with
the non-conversational commands (`sk workflows …`, `sk connectors …`,
`sk executions …`) or from your own machine over the API.

---

## Headless = the same loop, scripted

For CI or one-liners, `-p` runs one prompt non-interactively through the **same**
authoring engine (no TTY, no slash commands — the AI completes autonomously up to
`--max-turns`):

```bash
sk -p "create a workflow that returns the current temperature in Berlin using the open-meteo connector" \
   --output text --max-turns 40
sk -p "list my workflows" --output json
```

`--output {text|json|stream-json}` controls the shape; non-zero exit codes signal
failure so scripts can branch reliably.

<!-- Source: docs/authors/settings.md -->

<!-- generated by scripts/gen-sk-settings-doc.ts — do not edit by hand -->

# sk settings

Settings for the `sk` CLI itself — separate from the engine's runtime
settings (see [settings-reference](../admins/settings-reference.md)).
Open the in-REPL palette with `/settings`.

## Files

`sk` reads two files under `~/.sk`, plus per-project overlays:

| file | purpose |
| ---- | ------- |
| `~/.sk/settings.json` | User settings (the `SkSettings` shape below). |
| `~/.sk/config.json` | Multi-profile auth/connection config (the `SkConfig` shape below). |
| `<repo>/.sk/settings.json` | Project settings, walked upward from the cwd. |
| `<cwd>/.sk/settings.local.json` | Local, git-ignored overrides (highest precedence). |

Settings merge later-wins in that order. `config.json` is written with
`0600` permissions because it holds the API key.

## Settings (`~/.sk/settings.json`)

| field | type | default | description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `model` | string | — | Default model id for new conversations. |
| `defaultTenant` | string | — | Tenant id used when no `--tenant` / profile tenant is set. |
| `additionalDirectories` | string[] | — | Extra directories the session may read files from. |
| `mcpServers` | Record<string, { url?, command?, args? }> | — | External MCP servers to surface inside the session. |
| `includeMemoryFile` | boolean | `true` | Inject `SK.md` into each session. |
| `maxInlineMentionBytes` | number | `262144` | Max bytes inlined when an `@mention` expands a file. |
| `headless.maxTurns` | number | — | Cap on model/tool steps for one `sk -p` headless turn. |
| `headless.maxBudgetTokens` | number | — | Token budget ceiling for a headless turn. |
| `nextCommandPreviewEnabled` | boolean | `true` | Show the engine's next-message ghost-text preview after each turn. |

### Status line (`statusLine`)

Provide `command` to drive the line from a shell hook, or `format` for a
local template. The boolean/`refreshMs` fields tune the built-in line.

| field | type | default | description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `statusLine.command` | string | — | Shell command run per refresh; receives `StatusLineInput` JSON on stdin, its stdout becomes the line. |
| `statusLine.format` | string | — | Local template rendered when `command` is absent (placeholders below). |
| `statusLine.showCost` | boolean | `false` | Show cost in the default line. |
| `statusLine.showTokens` | boolean | `true` | Show token counters in the default line. |
| `statusLine.showPersona` | boolean | `true` | Show the resolved persona in the default line. |
| `statusLine.refreshMs` | number | `500` | Minimum milliseconds between status-line rebuilds. |

#### `statusLine.format` placeholders

Unknown placeholders expand to an empty string.

| placeholder | meaning |
| ----------- | ------- |
| `{persona}` | Resolved persona (admin / operator / member / enduser / portal). |
| `{tenant}` | Active tenant id. |
| `{model}` | Model id for the active conversation. |
| `{engine_url}` | Engine base URL. |
| `{session_id}` | Active conversation id. |
| `{turn_tokens}` | Tokens spent on the most recent turn. |
| `{remaining_tokens}` | Tokens left in the budget. |
| `{cwd}` | Current working directory. |
| `{git_branch}` | Current git branch. |

## Profiles (`~/.sk/config.json`)

`SkConfig` holds an `active_profile` (default `"default"`) and a
`profiles` map. Each `Profile` carries:

| field | type | default | description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `engine_url` | string | `"http://localhost:3000"` | Engine base URL for this profile. |
| `api_key` | string | — | Bearer API key (omitted when signed out). |
| `active_tenant_id` | string \| null | `null` | Tenant selected for this profile. |
| `persona_hint` | enum("admin","operator","member","enduser","portal") | — | Cached persona for status-line rendering; re-probed via RBAC on startup. |
| `portal_locked` | boolean | — | True for profiles authenticated via a portal token. |
| `notification_inbox_cursor` | number | — | Highest notification-inbox row id this profile has paged. |

Profile resolution precedence (later loses): CLI flags
(`--engine-url`, `--api-key`, `--tenant`, `--profile`) → env
(`SUBKIT_ENGINE_URL`, `SUBKIT_API_KEY`, `SUBKIT_TENANT`,
`SUBKIT_PROFILE` / `SK_PROFILE`) → on-disk profile fields → defaults.

# Slash commands

Slash commands run from the `sk` REPL. Type `/` to open the prefix
picker, or `/help` for the persona-filtered cheat sheet. A command
with a `requires` permission is hidden from any persona that cannot
invoke it — the engine still enforces the permission on every call,
so this column is the UX gate, not the security boundary.

## Session

| command | aliases | requires | description |
| ------- | ------- | -------- | ----------- |
| `/approvals` | — | `conversation:read` | Show approval history for the active conversation |
| `/approve` | — | `conversation:approve` | Approve a pending request_human_approval |
| `/clear` | `/new` | `conversation:write` | Start a new conversation |
| `/compact` | — | `conversation:write` | Compact the message history |
| `/connector` | — | `conversation:read` | Inspect the current connector draft |
| `/draft` | — | `conversation:read` | Inspect the current connector/workflow authoring state |
| `/edit` | — | `conversation:write` | Direct-edit the workflow draft (or one step) as JSON — `/edit [step]` writes the edit file, `/edit apply` submits it as a validated patch |
| `/fork` | — | `conversation:write` | Fork the current session into a new conversation |
| `/model` | — | `conversation:write` | Switch the conversation's model |
| `/onboard` | `/install` | `connector:write` | Launch an interactive onboarding wizard — pick a template, enter credentials, probe, save |
| `/policy` | — | `conversation:write` | List tool execution-mode badges, or pin a per-tool override. `/policy` lists; `/policy <tool> <auto\|ask\|review>` sets; `/policy <tool> reset` clears. |
| `/preview` | — | `conversation:write` | Dry-run the draft directly and show the result — `/preview [step]`; `/preview show` re-opens the last result |
| `/probe` | — | `conversation:write` | Probe the connector draft directly and show the result — `/probe [path]`; `/probe show` re-opens the last result |
| `/reject` | — | `conversation:approve` | Reject a pending approval (with optional reason) |
| `/rename` | — | `conversation:write` | Rename the current session — `/rename <new-title>` |
| `/restore` | — | `workflow:write` | Restore a workflow version — `/restore <version>` |
| `/resume` | — | `conversation:list` | Reattach to a previous conversation |
| `/snapshots` | — | `conversation:read` | Browse draft snapshots — `/snapshots` lists; `/snapshots restore [id]` rolls back (newest when omitted) |
| `/templates` | — | `conversation:read` | Browse connector templates suggested for the current draft |
| `/versions` | — | `workflow:read` | List the committed workflow versions for the current target |
| `/workflow` | — | `conversation:read` | Inspect the current workflow draft |
| `/yolo` | — | `conversation:write` | Arm yolo mode — lifts the destructive-action confirmation gate (typed `yes` confirmation; auto-disarms after 10 turns / 10 min). `/yolo off` disarms now. |

# Developers

Run sk on your own infrastructure and change it safely. Everything here takes you from a clone to a green test suite, a live engine on your own hardware, and a workflow you can reach from the CLI, a REST call, an MCP client, or your own code — all of them landing on the same permission and audit model, so you never secure a surface twice.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Q[quickstart.md] --> SH[self-host.md]
    SH --> IS[input-surfaces.md]
    IS --> TP[tool-palette.md]
    IS --> CLI[cli-reference.md]
    IS --> CA[coding-agent-integration.md]
    TP --> EP[evidence-process.md]
```

Start with **quickstart** for a green gate locally, then **self-host** to stand up your own engine. **input-surfaces** maps the doors in (CLI, REST, MCP), with **cli-reference** and **tool-palette** as the per-surface detail. **coding-agent-integration** turns sk into the knowledge source for Claude Code and Codex sessions. **evidence-process** is the bar for changing LLM-driven paths.

> Just want your own Claude Code grounded in your team's knowledge? You are not
> in the contributor lane — go to
> [Use sk from a coding agent](../authors/coding-agents.md).

| Page | What it covers | Link |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quickstart — Developer | Clone to a passing test suite and a live engine in ~10 minutes. | [quickstart.md](quickstart.md) |
| Self-Host sk — Zero to Running | Self-host the engine in your own infra with PostgreSQL, no SaaS lock-in. | [self-host.md](self-host.md) |
| Input Surfaces | The doors into the engine — CLI, REST, MCP, webhooks — over one RBAC and Audit model. | [input-surfaces.md](input-surfaces.md) |
| sk CLI reference | Non-interactive `sk` commands for scripting and CI. | [cli-reference.md](cli-reference.md) |
| Tool palette and dispatch | Every LLM action as a named, governed, audited tool. | [tool-palette.md](tool-palette.md) |
| Coding-agent integration | sk as the knowledge/skill source for Claude Code and Codex — briefing, capture, review, skills sync. | [coding-agent-integration.md](coding-agent-integration.md) |
| Evidence process | Verifying a behavioral / LLM-path change with proof, not guesses. | [evidence-process.md](evidence-process.md) |

# Detailed Agent Navigation

This on-demand reference preserves the former root agent guide. The compact root `AGENTS.md` is the always-loaded contract; consult this file only for the relevant subsystem.

# subkit Agent Guide

Canonical repo-wide instructions for coding agents working in this project.
Use this file as the default contract. `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `SKILLS.md`, and tool-specific
instruction files are compatibility layers or indexes — not competing sources of truth.

## Scope & invariants

- **subkit is a self-hostable, multi-tenant engine for governed, versioned, AI-assisted
  workflow execution.** It is not a chat product, not an LLM provider, and not a general
  workflow-automation tool. It owns: identity & access (RBAC/ABAC, encrypted credentials,
  portal tokens, API keys), unified data/tool interfaces (5 typed drivers, 56 connector
  templates), governed execution (append-only audit log, human-in-the-loop approvals,
  versioned workflows with full snapshots), observability (Prometheus, structured logs,
  drift detection), and multi-tenant conversation-first surfaces (CLI, `sk`, Slack, Teams,
  Google Chat, MCP).
- Every piece of state is **tenant-scoped**. Every row carries `tenant_id`. Do not add
  globals or cross-tenant reads without explicit RBAC + audit plumbing.
- **Audit everything that changes state.** Workflow commits, credential writes, approvals,
  skill promotions, schedule fires — all must produce an `audit_log` entry. The log is
  append-only because no code path writes or deletes one; it is not protected at the
  storage layer, so do not describe it as tamper-proof.
- **Skills are human-approved only.** Skill Candidates are proposed from execution patterns;
  they become Skills only through explicit operator action. Do not auto-promote.
- **A comment is a claim; only a test is evidence.** A comment may explain *why* this line
  is the way it is, state what must stay true here, or name the authority that proves a
  claim (a test path — `check:docs-refs` verifies it exists). It must **not** describe what
  another module, a client, or a test does: that assertion has nothing verifying it and
  goes stale silently. If you catch yourself writing "X does Y over there", write the test
  named after that sentence instead. The same discipline applies to `docs/`: an absolute
  claim ("cannot", "never", "always", "no X in the path") needs either a test behind it or
  the qualification that makes it true. Five comments in this repo have already asserted
  behaviour the code did not have — twice optimistic, three times the reverse.
- **Naming.** The prose docs describe the drift-repair subsystem as *drift-assisted repair*;
  the codebase keeps the technical name *self-healing* (directory
  `apps/engine/src/self-healing/`, module identifiers, log events) — do not rename it for
  vocabulary alignment. The same applies to `apps/engine/src/rbac/` and other stable
  identifiers.
- Keep public / documentation surfaces separate from authenticated engine routes.

## Canonical Sources

Read the smallest relevant set of sources before changing behavior.

Priority when sources conflict:

1. Code, types, tests, and verified inline decisions.
2. Canonical docs in `docs/` (numbered) and workflow/config files.
3. Existing implementation examples (e.g. the 57 templates, the 5 drivers).

High-value references (by task type):

- **Project shape & build** — `package.json`, `biome.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `docker-compose.yml`,
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.commitlintrc.json`
- **Platform & concepts** — `docs/concepts/glossary.md`
- **Input surfaces** — `docs/developers/input-surfaces.md`. The sk REPL exposes a 5-tab
  `/settings` palette (`Status · Config · Usage · Skills · Knowledge`) embedded
  in-process via the `kind: "settings"` PaneSpec. Operator surfaces
  (`Permissions`, `Profile`, `Admin`) are not tabs — each is its own SinglePane
  slash command (`/permissions`, `/profile`, `/admin`); `/admin` renders a
  "no admin permissions" message unless the principal holds an admin-scoped
  permission. Slash registry is in `apps/sk/src/slash.ts`; deleted-slash
  redirects in `apps/sk/src/repl/slash/dispatcher.ts:REMOVED_SLASH_GUIDANCE`.
- **AI authoring** — `docs/authors/authoring-workflows.md`
- **Connectors & integration** — `docs/concepts/connectors.md`
- **Execution** — `docs/concepts/workflows.md`
- **Security & governance** — `docs/concepts/governance-and-audit.md`
- **Operations** — `docs/operators/observability.md`
- **Agent-task navigation** — `.claude/docs/agent-navigation.md` (task-oriented index)

## Working Rules

- Start with the doc/spec that owns the behavior you are about to change. Do not reinvent
  an existing subsystem.
- **Configuration before deployment.** Workflow definitions, prompts, model
  parameters, per-run limits, and editorial policy are versioned runtime data.
  Change them through the existing workflow/settings/knowledge surfaces before
  considering engine code. Do not start a patch→release→deploy loop for each
  issue discovered during a user workflow; collect engine gaps and ship them
  later as one planned maintenance release unless the current goal is otherwise
  impossible.
- **Prove the release boundary first.** Before preparing a version bump, state
  why the existing workflow API, settings overrides/hot reload, or knowledge
  update path cannot achieve the requested result. Full CI/CD is a release
  gate, not an exploratory debugging loop.
- Prefer small, reviewable diffs that preserve existing architecture over broad rewrites.
- Put shared guidance in this file or a directory-local `AGENTS.md`, never in tool-specific shims.
- **Use `bun`, not `npm` or `yarn`.** Scripts assume the `bun` runtime.
- **Imports are ESM.** The project is `"type": "module"`. Use explicit extensions
  (`.ts` for source imports only if the existing code does; otherwise match file-local style).
- **Every HTTP boundary uses Zod schemas.** Add a `@hono/zod-openapi` schema for every
  route in `apps/engine/src/http/routes/` — inputs and outputs. OpenAPI is generated from Zod;
  do not hand-edit the OpenAPI surface.
- **Structured LLM flows use submit/abort.** `generate`, `extract`, `repair`, `discover`
  all call `AiSdkModel.generateObject` with `toolChoice:"required"` and a submit/abort
  tool pair, capped at `MAX_TOOL_LOOP_ATTEMPTS = 8`. Don't drop a flow back to
  text + best-effort JSON parsing — the eval gate (`verify:ai`) will catch it.
- **CLI parity with the conversational gates.** `sk workflows {validate, preview, create}`
  and `sk connectors {inspect, probe, create}` enforce the same
  `inspect → validate → preview/probe → commit/save` state machine the conversation loop
  enforces. `--skip-checks` is the only escape hatch; use it sparingly.
- **Dry-run warnings feed the next turn.** When `dry_run_workflow` / `dry_run_step`
  emit warnings (`unresolved_identifier`, rate limits, pagination edges), they land on
  `draft.latest_preview.warnings` and the loop folds them into the next turn's
  `prior_failures` automatically.
- **Use the structured logger** (`apps/engine/src/logging/`) in engine, CLI, agent, and `sk`
  code. Do not introduce raw `console.log / warn / error` there. Build scripts under
  `scripts/` may use console output.
- **Untrusted JavaScript runs in `quickjs-emscripten` sandboxes only.** Before-request hooks,
  transforms, and self-healing patches must use the sandbox facility in
  `apps/engine/src/sandboxes/` with interrupt budgets set.
- **Never commit secrets.** `.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key` are off-limits to agents. The pre-bash
  hook will refuse to read them.
- **Never bypass the audit log.** If a change mutates tenant-visible state, write an
  `audit_log` entry with request-source, actor, and structured diff.

## Chat-First Authoring Contract

Every conversation-driven authoring flow (Conversation, Discovery, Diagnosis/Repair) follows
these invariants. Engine prompts, tool palettes, and skills must reinforce them; never weaken
one to make the model "easier to drive".

- **Chat is the operator surface.** Every action a user can take in the product, the agent
  can take through a tool call. When asked to do something, the agent calls the matching
  tool — it does not instruct the user to run `sk` CLI commands, paste shell prompts, or
  open a separate UI. If the matching tool does not exist, the agent calls `cannot_help`
  with a chat-actionable `suggest_alternative`, never a CLI suggestion.
- **Proof before proposal.** Before `author_workflow` (or a repair-stage `propose_step`), run
  `probe_connector` to verify the credential resolves and the base URL responds. Skipping
  the probe is the largest single source of authoring-time errors.
- **Dry-run before first commit.** A brand-new workflow draft must pass
  `dry_run_workflow` or step-by-step `dry_run_step` before `save_workflow_draft`. An in-place
  re-commit on a persisted workflow needs a fresh `validate_draft`; a fresh dry-run is
  optional once the change is small and validated.
- **Repair-in-chat is a first-class authoring phase.** When a persisted workflow fails,
  the conversation enters diagnosis mode (`diagnose_latest_execution` → edit → validate →
  commit). The same `save_workflow_draft` tool that creates a workflow also updates a persisted
  one in place. There is no separate repair tool and no CLI fallback.
- **Approval gates are governance, not UX.** `ask_user_confirm(kind: "save_workflow_draft")`,
  `ask_user_confirm(kind: "external_write")`, and the patch-candidate approval flow are
  load-bearing. Do not invent escape hatches, `--skip-checks` flags, or "auto-commit if
  validated" shortcuts.
- **Never auto-promote.** Skill Candidates and Patch Candidates surface as proposals; they
  become active Skills / applied patches only via explicit operator action through their
  approval tools. This holds even when the candidate is classified `safe`.
- **Stale checkpoints block state-advancing moves.** A draft mutation invalidates later
  checkpoints (inspect → validate → probe / preview). The state machine enforces this;
  prompts and tools must respect it instead of routing around it.
- **`load_skill` is internal.** The agent loads skills silently and never narrates the
  load, names the skill in user-facing prose, or tells the user to read documentation.
- **Tenant snapshot before list_*.** Every converse turn carries a TENANT SNAPSHOT block
  with workflow + connector ids. Enumeration questions ("show my workflows", "welche
  connectoren habe ich") answer from the snapshot in zero tool calls. `list_*` tools are
  for pagination, filtered views, or explicit refresh — not double-checking.

## Architecture And Domain Safety

Preserve the current responsibility split. If you find yourself adding logic in the wrong
layer, stop and move it.

- **`apps/engine/`** — the server. All domain logic, HTTP routes, MCP server, queue workers,
  webhooks, scheduler, pub/sub, connector drivers, AI flows, self-healing, audit log.
- **`apps/sk/`** — the `sk` unified CLI (Ink-based TUI + citty subcommands). Persona-aware:
  end-users get the REPL; operators and admins get the full admin surface too. No domain logic.
- **`packages/cli-core/`** — shared CLI utilities (updater, version, prompts). Pure,
  reusable, no `apps/*` imports.
- **`packages/shared/`** — shared domain types & helpers. Pure, deterministic, no
  `apps/*` imports. See `packages/shared/AGENTS.md` for stricter rules.

Subsystem map inside `apps/engine/src/` (47 directories + 5 loose root files):

| Concern | Directory | Key docs |
|---|---|---|

| Top-level integration suites | `tests/` | (test infrastructure) |
| Cross-subsystem utilities | `utils/` | (shared helpers) |
| Inbound + outbound webhooks (incl. transactional outbox dispatch) | `webhooks/` | `docs/developers/input-surfaces.md` |
| Inbound signal write + atomic-claim match (wait-for-event step) | `workflow-signals/` | `docs/concepts/workflows.md` |
| Persistent per-workflow tenant-encrypted state (`state_read` / `state_write`) | `workflow-state/` | `docs/concepts/workflows.md` |
| DAG versioning + locking + execution | `workflows/` | `docs/concepts/workflows.md` |

Loose root files in `apps/engine/src/`:

- `index.ts` — process entry point.
- `env.ts` + `env.test.ts` — Zod-parsed env loader; the only place process.env reads happen at boot.
- `self-update.ts` + `update-state.ts` — engine self-update channel for dev.

Directory-local overrides:

- `apps/engine/AGENTS.md` — strict rules for engine code.
- `apps/sk/AGENTS.md` — `sk` unified CLI (Ink REPL + citty admin subcommands).
- `packages/shared/AGENTS.md` — pure/deterministic code only.

## Code Quality Enforcement

- **Biome** (`biome.json`) is the only formatter and linter. 100 char line width, 2-space
  indent, double quotes, semicolons, trailing commas. Run `bun run lint` before calling done.
- **TypeScript strict mode.** No `any` in new code. No non-null assertions without a
  documented invariant. Run `bun run typecheck` before calling done.
- **Zod at boundaries.** Every REST route, every MCP tool, every webhook, every CLI
  input — schema first.
- **Conventional commits** (`.commitlintrc.json`). Allowed types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`,
  `chore`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `style`, `revert`. Header ≤ 100 chars.
  They keep `CHANGELOG.md` readable when a release is cut by hand (bump version, tag `v<version>`, push).
- **No `console.*` in app/engine code.** Use the structured logger.
- **Inline comments explain WHY, not WHAT.** Remove any comment that restates what the
  function or variable name already says. Keep only non-obvious constraints, workarounds
  for specific bugs, and subtle invariants. One line max; no multi-line docblocks.
- **No ticket coupling in comments or docs.** Inline comments, `TODO`s, and docs must not
  reference PR numbers, issue IDs, `bug-N` labels, review-wave letters (`W1`, `S3`, `R2-W4`,
  `P0-1`), or round numbers. Either the invariant is permanent and belongs in code, or the
  follow-up is real and belongs in the issue tracker — not in source.

## Validation And Testing

Three test layers (picked by subsystem and command):

| Layer | Command | When | What runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| unit | `bun run test:unit` | Fast inner loop. Requires a running Postgres (compose) for the subset that uses `createTestDb`; otherwise no external dependencies. | `observability`, `logging`, `audit`, `llm`, `workflows`, `execution/tests` |
| integration | `bun run test:integration` | Needs Postgres + pg-boss (Docker Compose). | `db`, `queue`, `http`, `webhooks`, `credentials/oauth2` |
| e2e | `bun run test:e2e` | Compiles `sk` as needed and runs against a live engine. | `tests/e2e/` |
| eval | `bun run verify:ai` | Prompting, context assembly, routing, and authoring-contract changes. | `apps/engine/eval/*` |

- Unit tests co-located as `*.test.ts` alongside source.
- Integration tests use a disposable Postgres database per test file (`createTestDb`) against the running compose instance.
- E2E tests drive compiled CLIs — they will build them if missing.
- `bun run test:e2e` is the ONLY supported way to run the e2e layer, and it is what CI runs:
  it delegates to `scripts/test-e2e-isolated.ts`, one `bun test` process per file. Never run
  `bun test tests/e2e/` — that puts all e2e files in one process, where suites contend for
  process-global state (config leaves, env vars, LLM provider, pg-boss workers, listening
  servers) and roughly half the runs fail on interference unrelated to the change. A single
  file by name is fine: one file is one process.
- CI currently runs lint, typecheck, migrations, `bun test apps/ packages/`, `build:all`, e2e,
  engine smoke, and compose validation. The local `bun run verify` gate is stricter: it also runs
  the determinism lint and the AI/eval contract suite.

## Quality Gate Before Done

Before marking any code task done, run (or have a reason not to):

1. `bun run lint` — biome check, no warnings.
2. `bun run typecheck` — tsc clean.
3. `bun run test:determinism` — determinism lint clean.
4. `bun run test:unit` — unit tests green.
5. `bun run verify:ai` — eval fixtures green when the change touches prompting, context,
   routing, authoring, or verification behavior.
6. Integration/e2e where the change touches those layers (`test:integration`, `test:e2e`).
7. Verify audit log + Zod schemas were updated if the change mutates state or hits a
   route.

Or use the `/verify` command, which runs the full local release gate (`bun run verify`).

## Useful Commands

Day-to-day:

- `bun run dev` — engine in watch mode.
- `bun run lint` / `bun run lint:fix` / `bun run format`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run verify` / `bun run verify:ai` / `bun run eval`
- `bun run test:unit` / `bun run test:integration` / `bun run test:e2e`
- `bun run build:all` — compile all 3 repo binaries into `dist/`.

Database & infra:

- `bun run compose:up` / `compose:down` / `compose:reset` / `compose:logs` — Docker Compose.
- `bun run db:generate` — drizzle-kit generate.
- `bun run db:migrate` — apply migrations.
- `bun run db:seed` — seed dev data.
- `bun run db:issue-admin-key` — mint an admin API key locally.
- `bun run metrics` — curl `/metrics` from the running engine.

## Project Agent Files

Companion files live under `.claude/`:

- `.claude/CLAUDE.md` — Claude Code bootstrap shim; delegates here.
- `.claude/agents/` — specialist sub-agents (`domain-architect`, `connector-builder`,
  `test-generator`).
- `.claude/skills/` — project-local skills; see root `SKILLS.md` for the index.
- `.claude/commands/` — thin `/verify` and `/review` commands.
- `.claude/settings.json` + `.claude/hooks/pre-bash-dispatch.sh` — bash safety net.

Directory-local overrides:

- `apps/engine/AGENTS.md`
- `apps/sk/AGENTS.md`
- `packages/shared/AGENTS.md`

When in doubt, start here, then follow the most specific pointer downward.

# sk CLI reference

Every `sk` command and argument — and the surface authoring runs through:
creating or changing a workflow, connector, knowledge source or skill is a
definition edit, and definition edits belong here, where the change is a
file you can read and a command you can re-run.

Running bare `sk` opens the interactive REPL; every command below is
scriptable and prints to stdout. The declarative path — `create --file`,
`update --file`, `validate`, `preview` / `probe` — checks a definition
*before* it exists rather than after, so a mistake costs an error message
instead of a half-built connector someone has to clean up.

The `requires` column is the persona-aware *visibility* gate used for
`--help` filtering — the engine independently enforces permissions on
every API call.

| command | requires | description | subcommands |
| ------- | -------- | ----------- | ----------- |
| `sk agent` | `skill:read` | Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup | `briefing`, `capture`, `init` |
| `sk apikeys` | `api_key:read` | Manage API keys | `create`, `list`, `revoke`, `rotate` |
| `sk attach` | `file:write` | Upload a file and link it to a conversation (shortcut) | — |
| `sk audit` | `audit:read` | Query the append-only audit log | `export`, `query`, `show`, `tail` |
| `sk auth` | `connector:write` | Start a reauthentication flow for a connector (OAuth2 authorize URL). An mcp connector authorizes through `sk connectors mcp-authorize` instead — it discovers its authorization server rather than reading one from config. | — |
| `sk chat` | `chat_workspace:read` | Manage external chat spaces (Google Chat / Slack) | `install-space`, `remove-space`, `spaces` |
| `sk connector-templates` | `connector:read` | Manage connector templates | `create`, `delete`, `list`, `recipe`, `recipe-pack`, `recipes`, `search`, `set-oauth` |
| `sk connectors` | `connector:read` | Manage connectors | `create`, `delete`, `disable`, `docs-delete`, `docs-ingest`, `docs-list`, `docs-search`, `enable`, `get`, `import`, `inspect`, `list`, `mcp-authorize`, `mcp-inspect`, `patch`, `probe`, `promote`, `test`, `validate` |
| `sk credentials` | `credential:read` | Manage connector credentials | `delete`, `list`, `rotate`, `set` |

## Commands and arguments

Every argument of every command. `<name>` is positional; `--name` is a flag.

### `sk agent`

Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup

#### `sk agent briefing`

Print the domain-scoped session briefing for coding agents

- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .sk/agent.json of the repo)
- `--budget` (string) — Token budget for the briefing
- `--hook` (default: false) — SessionStart-hook mode: read hook JSON from stdin, never fail
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk agent capture`

Send a session transcript to the engine for learning distillation

- `--transcript` (string) — Path to the transcript file (JSONL or text)
- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .sk/agent.json of the repo)
- `--agent` (string, default: claude-code) — Producing agent name
- `--session-id` (string) — Session id for evidence attribution
- `--hook` (default: false) — SessionEnd/Stop-hook mode: read hook JSON from stdin, never fail
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk agent init`

Declare this repo's domains and wire coding-agent session hooks

- `--domains` (string, required) — Comma-separated domain slugs this repo grounds on (e.g. blog-de)
- `--budget` (string) — Optional per-session token budget
- `--skip-claude` (default: false) — Do not touch ~/.claude/settings.json


### `sk apikeys`

Manage API keys

#### `sk apikeys create`

Issue a new API key (shown once)

- `--name` (string) — Friendly key name (label)
- `--expires` (string) — Expiry — ISO-8601 timestamp
- `--scopes` (string) — Comma-separated scope strings (e.g. "workflow:read,workflow:invoke"). Defaults to ["*"] — full role-derived access, and read-and-execute over MCP. Add "mcp:authoring" for a key that may also author definitions over MCP (a coding agent); leave it off for a key going into a browser client.
- `--allowed-workflows` (string) — Comma-separated workflow ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".
- `--allowed-connectors` (string) — Comma-separated connector ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".

#### `sk apikeys list`

List API keys

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk apikeys revoke`

Revoke an API key

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Key id

#### `sk apikeys rotate`

Rotate an API key (new key shown once)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Key id


### `sk attach`

Upload a file and link it to a conversation (shortcut)

- `<conversation-id>` (positional, required) — Conversation id (UUID)
- `<path>` (positional, required) — Path to file
- `--content-type` (string) — Override detected MIME type
- `--slug` (string) — Optional slug for the link
- `--role` (string) — Optional role for the link
- `--quiet` (default: false) — Suppress progress output
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `sk audit`

Query the append-only audit log

#### `sk audit export`

Stream audit log as NDJSON to stdout or a file

- `--since` (string) — Lower bound — ISO-8601 timestamp
- `--output` (string) — Output file path (default: stdout)

#### `sk audit query`

Filter the audit log

- `--limit` (string) — Max rows
- `--since` (string) — Lower bound — ISO-8601 timestamp or relative (e.g. 10m, 1h, 7d)
- `--action` (string) — Action name filter
- `--actor` (string) — Actor id filter
- `--resource-id` (string) — Filter by resource id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk audit show`

Fetch one audit event by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Audit event id

#### `sk audit tail`

Follow new audit events via SSE stream

_No arguments._


### `sk auth`

Start a reauthentication flow for a connector (OAuth2 authorize URL). An mcp connector authorizes through `sk connectors mcp-authorize` instead — it discovers its authorization server rather than reading one from config.

- `--connector-id` (string, required) — Connector to reauthenticate
- `--json` — Emit the full response as JSON


### `sk chat`

Manage external chat spaces (Google Chat / Slack)

#### `sk chat install-space`

Register a chat space with the engine (Google Chat / Slack)

- `<platform>` (positional) — google_chat | slack
- `<workspace_id>` (positional) — Native space id, e.g. spaces/<id> (Slack: team id T…)
- `--bot-token` (string) — Slack bot token (xoxb-…) — required for slack
- `--default-channel` (string) — Optional default channel
- `--as` (string) — Installer platform user id (auto-filled from a pending space when omitted)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk chat remove-space`

Remove a chat-space install

- `<id>` (positional) — Chat workspace row id
- `--yes` — Skip confirmation
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk chat spaces`

List chat spaces installed in this tenant

- `--json` — JSON output


### `sk connector-templates`

Manage connector templates

#### `sk connector-templates create`

Create a connector template

- `--file` (string) — Path to a full template JSON file
- `--slug` (string) — Template slug (short-form convenience mode)
- `--name` (string) — Template name (short-form convenience mode)
- `--driver` (string) — Driver identifier (short-form convenience mode)

#### `sk connector-templates delete`

Delete a connector template

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Template id

#### `sk connector-templates list`

List connector templates

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connector-templates recipe`

Show one recipe by slug (template slug + recipe slug)

- `<slug>` (positional) — Template slug (e.g. stripe)
- `<recipe>` (positional) — Recipe slug (e.g. list-customers)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connector-templates recipe-pack`

Show the recipes in a vertical pack

- `<vertical>` (positional) — Vertical (revops | customer-success | finance | data | devops | security | marketing | hr)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connector-templates recipes`

List recipes shipped with a connector template

- `<slug>` (positional) — Template slug (e.g. stripe, github)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connector-templates search`

Fuzzy-search connector templates by name/alias/keyword

- `<query>` (positional, required) — Search text (e.g. 'hub')
- `--limit` (string, default: 10) — Max results
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connector-templates set-oauth`

Store tenant-scoped OAuth client credentials for a connector template

- `--slug` (string, required) — Template slug
- `--client-id` (string, required) — OAuth client id
- `--client-secret` (string, required) — OAuth client secret


### `sk connectors`

Manage connectors

#### `sk connectors create`

Create a connector from a template slug (--template) or a definition file (--file). --file runs validate and probe against the unsaved definition first, so a broken connector is never created; pass --skip-checks to bypass.

- `--template` (string) — Template slug
- `--file` (string) — Path to a connector definition JSON file
- `--credential` (string) — Path to a credential JSON file used to sign the pre-save probe. Never stored — attach the credential with `sk credentials set` after create.
- `--name` (string) — Override connector name (--template only)
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the checks (NOT recommended).
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `sk connectors delete`

Delete a connector

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id
- `--yes` — Skip confirmation

#### `sk connectors disable`

Disable a connector. It keeps its configuration and credentials and stops being offered for use.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `sk connectors docs-delete`

Delete a connector doc

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `<doc-id>` (positional, required) — Doc id

#### `sk connectors docs-ingest`

Ingest docs from a URL into a connector

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--url` (string, required) — URL to ingest

#### `sk connectors docs-list`

List ingested docs for a connector

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connectors docs-search`

Ranked search over connector docs

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `<query>` (positional, required) — Search query
- `--limit` (string, default: 10) — Max results

#### `sk connectors enable`

Enable a connector (operator on switch)

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `sk connectors get`

Get a connector by id

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `sk connectors import`

Turn an API specification into a connector. Parses the spec, shows the draft it produced, then creates it after confirmation (--yes to skip). Nothing is saved until you agree.

- `--spec` (string, required) — Path to the specification file, or a URL / curl command (see --source)
- `--source` (string, required) — openapi | google_discovery | postman | har | graphql | graphql_introspection | curl
- `--name` (string) — Override the connector name
- `--environment` (string) — dev (default) or prod
- `--yes` — Create without asking (for non-interactive use)
- `--dry-run` — Print the draft and stop. Nothing is created.
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `sk connectors inspect`

Inspect a connector resource (alias of `get`).

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `sk connectors list`

List connectors, grouped into catalog blocks

- `--limit` (string, default: 50) — Max rows
- `--category` (string) — Only this catalog block. A connector's block is its driver: http, graphql, postgres, s3, mcp.
- `--flat` — One flat table instead of grouped blocks
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connectors mcp-authorize`

mcp driver: begin the interactive OAuth 2.1 flow and print the URL to open in a browser.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `sk connectors mcp-inspect`

mcp driver: force one handshake and list the tools, capabilities and instructions the remote actually serves.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `sk connectors patch`

Update a connector, from --file (a partial definition: only the fields it names change) or from --name. --file runs validate first.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--file` (string) — Path to a partial definition JSON file
- `--name` (string) — New name
- `--skip-checks` — Skip validation (NOT recommended).
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `sk connectors probe`

Probe a connector's upstream boundary. With an id, probes the saved connector (alias of `test`); with --file, probes an unsaved definition and saves nothing.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id
- `--file` (string) — Path to a connector definition JSON file — probes it without saving it
- `--credential` (string) — Path to a credential JSON file. Signs this probe only; never stored. Required when the definition's auth_type is not 'none'.
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `sk connectors promote`

Promote a connector and its credentials from DEV to PROD

- `<id>` (positional) — DEV connector id
- `--to` (string, default: prod) — Target environment (prod only)
- `--strategy` (string, default: copy) — Promotion strategy: copy or move
- `--idempotency-key` (string) — Stable retry key; generated when omitted
- `--yes` — Confirm a move without prompting
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connectors test`

Test a connector connection (alias of `probe`). Exits non-zero when the probe fails.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `sk connectors validate`

Check a connector definition file against its driver's config schema. Saves nothing, reaches no upstream.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to a definition JSON file
- `--json` — JSON-only output


### `sk credentials`

Manage connector credentials

#### `sk credentials delete`

Delete a credential

- `<credential-id>` (positional, required) — Credential id

#### `sk credentials list`

List credentials for a connector

- `<connector-id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk credentials rotate`

Rotate a credential

- `<credential-id>` (positional, required) — Credential id

#### `sk credentials set`

Attach a credential to a connector (scriptable; no conversation needed). Modes: bearer | header | query | basic | aws_sigv4 | none.

- `<connector-id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--mode` (string, required) — bearer | header | query | basic | aws_sigv4 | none
- `--token` (string) — Secret token (bearer mode)
- `--header` (string) — header mode: "Name=Value" (comma-separate multiple)
- `--query` (string) — query mode: "key=Value" (comma-separate multiple)
- `--username` (string) — basic mode username
- `--password` (string) — basic mode password
- `--access-key-id` (string) — aws_sigv4 access key id
- `--secret-access-key` (string) — aws_sigv4 secret access key
- `--session-token` (string) — aws_sigv4 optional STS session token
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the post-set connectivity probe
- `--json` — JSON-only output


### `sk diagnostics`

Engine diagnostics: errors, LLM status, setup validation

#### `sk diagnostics errors`

Show recent engine errors

- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows
- `--since` (string) — ISO timestamp lower bound
- `--trace-id` (string) — Filter by trace id
- `--tail` — Keep reading (not applicable — uses snapshot endpoint)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk diagnostics llm`

Show LLM diagnostics

_No arguments._

#### `sk diagnostics setup`

Validate engine setup

- `--json` — JSON output

### `sk executions`

Manage workflow executions

#### `sk executions abort`

Abort a running execution

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id

#### `sk executions get`

Get an execution by id

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON-only (skip Output files line)

#### `sk executions list`

List executions

- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows
- `--status` (string) — Filter by status
- `--source` (string) — Filter by request source (e.g. scheduler, cli, api, mcp, chat)
- `--parent` (string) — Lineage filter: list the reruns spawned from this execution id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk executions rerun`

Re-run a previous execution against the workflow + input it carried. Useful after diagnose/repair.

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id to rerun
- `--input` (string) — Override the original input (JSON string). Omit to reuse it verbatim.
- `--follow` — Queue the rerun and stream its progress live (step-by-step JSON lines).

#### `sk executions result`

Print the final output a workflow execution produced

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON-only output

#### `sk executions steps`

List steps for an execution

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk executions tail`

Stream live output from an execution

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id

### `sk files`

Manage files (upload, download, link, …)

#### `sk files delete`

Soft-delete a file

- `<id>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `--force` (default: false) — Skip confirmation prompt

#### `sk files download`

Download a file by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `--output` (string) — Output path (default: ./<filename>, '-' for stdout)
- `--quiet` (default: false) — Suppress progress output

#### `sk files get`

Show file metadata

- `<id>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk files link`

Attach a file to an owning resource (conversation, knowledge_source, …)

- `<fid>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `--to` (string, required) — Owning resource as <resource_type>:<id>
- `--slug` (string) — Optional slug for the link
- `--role` (string) — Optional role for the link

#### `sk files list`

List files

- `--status` (string) — Filter by status (pending|ready|failed|…)
- `--linked-to` (string) — Filter to files linked to <type>:<id> (e.g. conversation:abc-…)
- `--cursor` (string) — Pagination cursor
- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows (1-100)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk files stats`

Aggregate file counters for this tenant

- `--by` (string) — Group by: status|scanner_verdict (default: status)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk files upload`

Upload a file (inline ≤5 MB, authenticated streaming above)

- `<path>` (positional, required) — Path to file
- `--content-type` (string) — Override detected MIME type
- `--no-dedup` (default: false) — Skip the client-side sha256 dedup probe (forces an upload)
- `--link-to` (string) — After upload, link the file to <resource_type>:<id>
- `--slug` (string) — Optional slug for the link
- `--role` (string) — Optional role for the link
- `--label` (string) — Reserved for future labels (no-op today)
- `--quiet` (default: false) — Suppress progress output
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output (also silences progress)

### `sk knowledge-sources`

Manage knowledge sources

#### `sk knowledge-sources analyze`

Generate a description + tags for a knowledge source via the engine LLM

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id
- `--force` (default: false) — Overwrite an existing description

#### `sk knowledge-sources create`

Upload a file as a knowledge source

- `--file` (string, required) — Path to file
- `--title` (string) — Override title (defaults to filename)
- `--description` (string) — Description (omit to let the engine auto-generate one)
- `--tags` (string) — Comma-separated tags. When set, they are authoritative (no AI auto-tagging). Omit both --tags and --description to auto-generate them.
- `--scope` (string) — Scope: global | workflow
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Workflow id (required when scope=workflow)
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `sk knowledge-sources delete`

Delete a knowledge source

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id

#### `sk knowledge-sources get`

Get a knowledge source by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id

#### `sk knowledge-sources import`

Import a directory of markdown files as one knowledge source (upsert by slug; OKF-compatible frontmatter is read tolerantly)

- `<dir>` (positional, required) — Directory to import
- `--name` (string) — Source name (defaults to root index.md H1 or dirname)
- `--slug` (string) — Stable slug (defaults to slugified name)
- `--description` (string) — Source description
- `--tags` (string) — Comma-separated extra tags (frontmatter tags merge in)
- `--scope` (string) — Scope: global | workflow
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Workflow id (required when scope=workflow)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk knowledge-sources list`

List knowledge sources

- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk knowledge-sources patch`

Update a knowledge source

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id
- `--title` (string) — New title
- `--description` (string) — New description
- `--tags` (string) — Comma-separated tags (replaces existing)
- `--status` (string) — Status: active | inactive

#### `sk knowledge-sources search`

Semantic search across knowledge sources

- `<query>` (positional, required) — Search query
- `--tags` (string) — Comma-separated tags to narrow results
- `--limit` (string, default: 10) — Max results
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

### `sk login`

Authenticate against a subkit engine

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL

- `--scope` (string) — OIDC scope override


### `sk logout`

### `sk logs`

Tail the engine's runtime log ring. --follow streams via SSE; --since accepts 5m / 2h / 1d / ISO-8601.

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key (audit:read required)
- `--profile` (string) — Use a named profile
- `--follow` (alias -f) — Live SSE tail (Ctrl-C to stop)
- `--since` (string) — Start time — relative (5m, 2h, 1d), ISO-8601, or unix-ms
- `--limit` (string) — Max entries when not following (default 200)
- `--module` (string) — Filter by module name (e.g. migrate, scheduler)
- `--action` (string) — Filter by action (e.g. drift_detected)
- `--level` (string) — Minimum level (trace|debug|info|warn|error|fatal)
- `--json` — Emit raw NDJSON for piping to jq, instead of pretty-printing

- `--executionMode` (string, default: prod) — Connector environment: dev or prod (default prod)

- `--input` (string) — JSON input payload passed to every run
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk schedules resume`

Resume a paused schedule

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Schedule id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk schedules update`

Update a schedule's cron, timezone, environment, or input

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Schedule id
- `--cron` (string) — New cron expression
- `--timezone` (string) — New IANA timezone
- `--executionMode` (string) — New connector environment: dev or prod

- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

### `sk settings`

List, read, write, or interactively configure engine settings (secrets always masked)

#### `sk settings configure`

Interactive Ink palette for inspecting settings (← / → cycles tabs, type to filter in Config, Enter to edit, Esc to exit). In non-TTY environments use --non-interactive to print the JSON contract instead.

- `--tab` (string) — Open directly on a tab: Status | Config | Usage | Skills | Knowledge
- `--non-interactive` — Skip the Ink renderer; print the GET /v1/settings response as JSON. Auto-detected when stdin is not a TTY.
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--tenant` (string) — Tenant id (writes a tenant overlay)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk settings get`

Read one leaf by dotted path

- `<path>` (positional, required) — Setting path (e.g. llm.api_key)
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--tenant` (string) — Tenant id (writes a tenant overlay)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk settings list`

List every leaf with its resolved value

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--tenant` (string) — Tenant id (writes a tenant overlay)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk settings set`

Write one leaf. <value> must be valid JSON ('"abc"', 42, true, null).

- `<path>` (positional, required) — Setting path
- `<value>` (positional, required) — Value as JSON
- `--force` — Bypass requiresRestart guard in production
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--tenant` (string) — Tenant id (writes a tenant overlay)
- `--json` — JSON output
